subject: Tier consolidation question — Compact -> Elastic and feature parity
messages:
From: Jordan Matthis <jordan.matthis@argushealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compact -> Elastic: feature parity and migration costs

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. Before we bring this to our engineering and procurement teams I need to clarify a couple of packaging items so we can model cost and risk:

- Feature parity: our product uses the "query-prioritization" and "prefix-caching" features that you demoed on Compact. If we move to Elastic (the throughput-focused tier) will those features be available or gated to specific addon bundles?
- Migration economics: we have a current 12-month commitment on Compact. If we want to move to Elastic mid-contract, is there a pro-rated credit, or will we need to do a separate commit?
- Pilot: can we run a 60-day pilot on Elastic with our production traffic pattern (bursting to 1,500 rps) without full commitment? If so, any limits we should model?

Procurement may ask for an initial SOW and a rough TCO spreadsheet. Can you send a single-page recommendation and a pricing worksheet we can forward?

Appreciate any clear guidance — Jordan
Jordan Matthis
Head of AI Integrations, Argus Health
--
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Matthis <jordan.matthis@argushealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compact -> Elastic: feature parity and migration costs

Jordan — thanks for the good questions. I pulled together an initial recommendation and a pricing workup (attached) to make the tradeoffs explicit. High-level answers up front:

1) Feature parity: Elastic includes the core runtime capabilities (KV/prefix caching, query-prioritization) but we package some advanced observability and cost-guardrails as optional feature bundles on Elastic. These are "Feature Packs" (Observability+, CostGuard) rather than hard gating. For Argus I recommend including Observability+ during pilot so you can validate token-level cost and latency.

2) Migration economics: We offer a "migration credit" model. If you move from Compact to Elastic before your Compact term ends, we provide a pro-rated credit of unused Compact commitment toward Elastic, plus a one-time migration credit equal to 10% of your remaining committed spend. That credit applies if you agree to a minimum 6-month Elastic commit.

3) Pilot: We can do a 60-day pilot on Elastic for production traffic at your burst profile. Pilot constraints: burst CPU priority vs guaranteed throughput — during pilot we provision a "pilot pool" that will cover sustained bursts up to ~1,800 rps but not guaranteed at the Dedicated level. If you need hard latency SLAs during pilot we recommend a short Dedicated add-on for the first 30 days.

Attached: Argus_pricing_workup.xlsx — includes three scenarios (pilot-only, 6mo commit, 12mo commit) and a line for feature-pack opt-ins.

Next steps: if that looks good I can loop in Ben (discount authority) and Lauren (CS) for an official pilot proposal + SOW. Also happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Rafael Mendes

Rafael — thanks for the quick reply and the spreadsheet. A few follow-ups from our side:

- Observability+: what telemetry is retained and for how long? We need token-level cost mapping for audits (minimum 90 days retention).
- The 10% migration credit sounds reasonable; procurement will want that in writing in the SOW along with the mechanic for pro-ration.
- Can you confirm whether the pilot pool will be single-tenant (dedicated) or multi-tenant? Procurement has a security checklist and needs to know whether traffic ever leaves our VPC.

Procurement: copying you on the thread — we need a draft SOW and an initial quote to start the procurement review.

Jordan

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Compact -> Elastic: feature parity and migration costs — pricing ask and SOW

Team — forwarding Argus's follow-ups. Two quick asks:

1) Discount authority: Jordan called out the 10% migration credit (we proposed). Ben — do we need legal signoff on the exact pro-rate mechanic or is commercial OK to propose this in the SOW? Recommended structure: pro-rate remaining Compact committed dollars over remaining months, apply that as a credit to Elastic invoice; plus one-time 10% credit applied against first Elastic invoice.

2) Pilot isolation: Kimberly / Lauren — what's our standard wording for a pilot pool that is logically isolated (priority) but remains on shared infra vs a short Dedicated add-on? Argus explicitly asked if traffic leaves their VPC. If they need VPC-peering (private deployment), that's a separate Private deal. For now I want to offer them a pilot variant that keeps KV/prefix cache reserved and Observability+ at 90-day retention.

If commercial can sign off I'll prepare a one-page SOW and redline (I'll attach SOW draft) and send to procurement.

Thanks — Rafael

Jordan / Procurement — thanks for the questions and the patience while I pulled approvals together. Summary of what we can offer and next steps: 

Offer summary (pilot -> commit path)
- 60-day Elastic pilot provisioned as a "pilot pool" with reserved KV/prefix cache capacity and Observability+ enabled. Observability+ retention: 90 days (token-level cost mapping included).
- Pilot pool will run on our multi-tenant Elastic fleet with logical priority and reserved cache — traffic will not be placed into your VPC for the pilot (no VPC peering). If you require VPC isolation we can switch to Private deployment but that is outside the pilot scope and requires a separate contract.
- Migration economics: pro-rated credit of unused Compact committed dollars applied to Elastic invoices + one-time migration credit of 10% of remaining Compact commitment. The migration credit is conditional on signing a new minimum 6-month Elastic commit within 30 days of pilot completion.
- Pricing: attached SOW & pricing workup. For a 6-month commit we are offering an introductory 12% effective discount on the Elastic baseline for Argus (reflected in the attached sheet). This requires Ben's approval (cc'd) and will be included in the SOW.

Attachments: SOW_draft_rafael_redline.docx, Argus_pricing_workup.xlsx

Next steps:
1) Procurement: review attached SOW and confirm procurement contact and PO mechanics. If you want VPC/private deployment we can scope that in parallel.
2) Pilot kickoff: propose week of May 22 for provisioning; we will need a 1-hour kickoff with your platform team to share traffic profile and API keys.
3) Legal/commercial: Ben and Kimberly will prepare final SOW and an amendment with the migration-credit mechanics.

Jordan — happy to jump on a 30-min call Monday to walk the SOW and the pilot constraints. If procurement needs a doc for their security review I can attach our standard security packet (SOC2 report, network diagram).
